source.title: Decomposing Prediction Mechanisms for In-Context Recall
source.authors: Sultan M. Daniels; Dylan Davis; Dhruv Gautam; Wentinn Liao; G. Ranade; Anant Sahai

page_placements.theme: Developmental order: induction heads relative to other circuits and abilities

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some mathematical notation and figures are flattened or imperfectly rendered, but the study is identifiable and readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies distinct mechanisms and learning dynamics for interleaved time-series recall and translation ICL. It cites work on induction heads but does not measure or test induction heads or their proposed relationship to ICL.
record.gate_note: The paper reports substantial results on related ICL tasks, but none directly measures induction heads or the specific token-copying behavior in the claim. The findings below are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study never identifies, measures or ablates induction heads or previous-token heads. Its edge-pruning circuits are not characterised as induction or previous-token heads. Its training-dynamics results concern continuous-state associative recall of linear systems and OLMo-2 translation accuracy, not the [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying behaviour. Induction heads appear only in cited related work, so none of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that next-token prediction in their toy task uses at least two separately emerging mechanisms: label-based recall for the first token, and a suboptimal observation-based Bayesian strategy for later tokens. They report an analogous first-token vs second-token gap in OLMo-2. They also find that emergence across model sizes aligns at a common pretraining-loss threshold. They draw no conclusion about induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates in-context recall of interleaved linear dynamical systems, prunes task-specific circuits, and tests translation prompts; it does not apply the original induction-head method.
record.method_sensitivity: The timing and performance vary with the number of systems in the haystack; semantic versus symbolic task labels change first-token performance. The paper also reports results under altered or synchronized symbolic labels in its out-of-distribution experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: In the synthetic interleaved-system task, first-system ICL improves gradually, while restarting ICL and first-token recall emerge abruptly at different times. Later-position predictions improve earlier than first-position recall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initiating and continuing an in-context-recalled sequence are separate mechanisms with separate emergence times.

fits_no_version.finding: Edge-pruned 1-after and 2-after circuits share 0% of their edges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuits for the first and second token of a resumed sequence are mechanistically distinct in this toy setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In OLMo-2 7B with symbolic labels, first-token translation accuracy jumps around 50k steps while second-token accuracy rises gradually. Semantic labels erase the gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task initiation from in-context demonstrations emerges later than task continuation in pretrained LLMs.

record.problems: The principal mechanistic experiments use a synthetic task. The edge-pruning analysis uses one haystack trace configuration and an earlier training run with a non-uniform orthogonal-matrix distribution. The OLMo translation evaluation uses 100 samples per evaluation point; several detailed training trajectories are shown in figures rather than tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed out-of-distribution misdirection and synchronization results in Section 4.1 were not extracted as rows because they test the synthetic task’s label-based versus observation-based recall mechanisms, not induction-head behavior or any specified claim version. Additional figure trajectories and appendix model-size plots were likewise omitted for the same reason.

untested.parts: All: no induction or previous-token heads are identified, and the pruned circuits are not characterised in those terms.
All: phase transitions are reported for recall and translation abilities, not tied to induction-head formation or a loss bump.
All: no attribution of in-context learning to induction heads.
All: data and training effects are shown on recall emergence, not on induction-head formation.
All: the first-token vs second-token mechanism split is not related to induction heads.
All: multiple separate transitions are shown for task abilities, not for induction-head formation.

record.verdict_notes: The Section 6 pretraining-loss threshold results, the model-size emergence results, and the Appendix D OLMo 'Z:' misdirection result are not rows. None bears on an induction-head version, so they are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head formation, composition with a previous-token head, and the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
Whether induction heads form alongside a gain in ICL or a bump in training loss.
Whether induction heads carry most loss-based ICL in large transformers.
Whether induction behavior is universal across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
How data or training setup affects induction-head formation or persistence of the specified ICL behavior.
Whether induction heads are or are not the main carrier of few-shot task learning.
Whether induction-head formation itself consists of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Medium
rows.stage_stated: trained GPT-2-style transformer; checkpoint at 6.25 × 10^7 training examples
rows.operation_detail: Measured median squared-error over context positions on held-out uninterleaved sequences during training.

conditions.value: in-context learning of the first system in the sequence
100 held-out systems and 1000 held-out initial states

rows.measure: Median squared-error by context index and training progress
rows.baseline: Pseudoinverse predictor; its errors are plotted for comparison
rows.value: After 6.25 × 10^7 training examples, prediction errors on indices 2 through 7 closely match the pseudoinverse baseline; final-context median squared-error is ≈ 2 × 10−4.
rows.uncertainty: 25th and 75th percentiles are not reported for this result in the text; figure shows median curves.
rows.note: The authors explicitly describe this first-system ICL ability as developing gradually, unlike the abrupt recall transitions they report elsewhere. This is an adjacent task, not the claim’s induction-head behavior.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Medium
rows.operation_detail: Measured median squared-error for predictions in a new system segment at different points in training.

conditions.value: restart ICL for a new system
third system segment in the haystack

rows.measure: Median squared-error for steps 1 through 8 in the segment
rows.baseline: First system segment’s corresponding prediction errors
rows.value: The third-segment errors converge toward the first-segment counterparts; the text places the transition toward correct restarting at ≈ 2 × 10^6 training examples.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show 25th and 75th percentiles across trace configurations; text gives no numerical interval.
rows.note: This measures restarting a continuous-state prediction task, not induction-head formation.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Medium
rows.operation_detail: Measured recall performance while varying training progress on needle-in-a-haystack traces.

conditions.value: first observation after the final open symbol

rows.baseline: Prediction after the initial open symbol in the haystack, shown as a comparator
rows.value: The recall transition begins at ≈ 1.5 × 10^7 training examples.
rows.uncertainty: 25th, 50th, and 75th quartiles are plotted; no numerical interval is stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors describe the first-observation recall curve as remaining high and then dropping. The subject is associative recall of linear-system states, not token-copy induction.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Medium
rows.operation_detail: Measured recall performance while varying training progress on needle-in-a-haystack traces.

conditions.value: first observation after the final open symbol

rows.baseline: Prediction after the initial open symbol in the haystack, shown as a comparator
rows.value: The transition is described as occurring closer to 2.5 × 10^7 training examples.
rows.uncertainty: 25th, 50th, and 75th quartiles are plotted; no numerical interval is stated in the text.
rows.note: The reported onset differs from the N = 1 condition. The authors characterize this as associative recall of systems, not induction-head formation.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Medium
rows.operation_detail: Compared training dynamics for the first and later predictions in a recalled sequence.

conditions.value: first, second, third, seventh, and eighth observations after the final open symbol

rows.baseline: First-observation recall trajectory, plotted alongside later-position trajectories
rows.value: The authors report that the first observation’s recall ability develops much later and more abruptly than the subsequent observations; later-position errors improve during training before the first-position recall transition.
rows.uncertainty: 25th, 50th, and 75th quartiles are plotted; no numerical interval is stated in the text.
rows.note: This is a token-position difference in a synthetic state-prediction task, not evidence about induction heads.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Sys 1-after Circuit
rows.stage_stated: pruned circuit from an earlier training run
rows.operation_detail: Applied edge pruning, quantized learned gates, and evaluated the resulting circuit.
rows.measure: Mean squared-error; number of edges in the circuit
rows.baseline: Full model: 32936 edges; errors 0.002 for 1-after and 0.004 for 2-after
rows.note: The study reports 0% edge overlap between the separately pruned 1-after and 2-after circuits, and describes their mechanisms as mostly distinct. The table’s reported error values are retained here; this does not test induction heads.
rows.check: 'partial' is meaningless with no linked version. The row reports a pruned circuit's errors against the full model (0.01 vs 0.002 at 1-after; 0.64 vs 0.004 at 2-after). It is a circuit-sparsity result, not an effect state for any version.

rows.subject: Orthogonal Sys 2-after Circuit
rows.stage_stated: pruned circuit from an earlier training run
rows.operation_detail: Applied edge pruning, quantized learned gates, and evaluated the resulting circuit.
rows.measure: Mean squared-error; number of edges in the circuit
rows.baseline: Full model: 32936 edges; errors 0.002 for 1-after and 0.004 for 2-after
rows.note: This separately pruned circuit has 0% edge overlap with the 1-after circuit. The paper notes that pruning used one trace configuration and that the model came from an earlier, non-uniform orthogonal-matrix training run.
rows.check: Same issue as R6. Pruned 2-after circuit errors (0.32 / 0.02) are not graded against any claim version.

rows.subject: OLMo-2 7B checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Measured translation accuracy by output-token position across training checkpoints in a two-shot prompting task.
rows.measure: Accuracy on first versus second task token
rows.baseline: First-token performance compared with second-token performance
rows.value: The first-token task has a phase transition around 50k training steps; second-token performance is better and improves more gradually.
rows.uncertainty: 95% credible intervals using Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5, 0.5), based on 100 samples per evaluation point.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a difference between initiating and continuing a prompted task. This is not a measurement of induction heads or repeated-token copying.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Fig. 21 right, pp. 18: first-token transition around 50k steps; second-token performance improves more gradually. Caption specifies two-shot prompting and 95% Jeffreys-prior credible intervals.

rows.subject: OLMo-2 7B checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Compared translation performance with semantic task labels against performance with symbolic task labels.
rows.measure: Accuracy on first versus second task token
rows.baseline: Symbolic-label in-context task from Fig. 21 right
rows.value: The first-token performance improves enough to erase the gap to second-token performance.
rows.uncertainty: 95% credible intervals using Jeffreys prior Beta(0.5, 0.5), based on 100 samples per evaluation point.
rows.note: The authors conclude the model can start translation when given semantic labels, but has difficulty recognizing from the symbolic demonstrations that translation is the task.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Fig. 21 left, p. 18: replacing symbolic labels with Spanish:/English: improves first-token performance and erases the gap.
